source.author: ov
source.text: Qui postquam senior regnumque aevumque peregit, exstinctum Latiaeque nurus populusque patresque deflevere Numam; nam coniunx urbe relicta vallis Aricinae densis latet abdita silvis sacraque Oresteae gemitu questuque Dianae impedit: a! quotiens nymphae nemorisque lacusque, ne faceret, monuere et consolantia verba dixerunt.
source.text_original: Qui postquam senior regnumque aevumque peregit, / exstinctum Latiaeque nurus populusque patresque / deflevere Numam; nam coniunx urbe relicta / vallis Aricinae densis latet abdita silvis / sacraque Oresteae gemitu questuque Dianae / impedit: a! quotiens nymphae nemorisque lacusque, / ne faceret, monuere et consolantia verba / dixerunt.
source.text_english: When he had lived out his old age and his reign, the people, the mothers-in-law of Latium, and the fathers all wept for Numa when he was gone; for his wife, having left the city, lies hidden in the Aricine valley, concealed in the dense woods, and she hinders Diana’s rites with the groan and lament of Orestes: ah, how often the nymphs and the lakes of the grove warned her not to do it, and spoke words of comfort.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: populumne levem veterique tyranno infensum atque olim miserantes Aesona patres advocet?
reuse.text_original: populumne levem veterique tyranno / infensum atque olim miserantes Aesona patres / advocet?
reuse.text_english: Should he summon a fickle people, hostile to the old tyrant, and the fathers of Aeson, who long ago had pity?
